title: HPA/KEDA signal alignment failure causing intermittent overprovisioning and cold-start churn
creator: Priya Sharma
summary: During a spike in short-lived inference bursts on hosted API routes, the cluster experienced repeated oscillatory scale-ups and scale-downs driven by a misalignment between KEDA scaler sampling windows and HPA aggregation. This caused repeated cold-starts for a subset of model shard pods, increased 95th-percentile latency by ~320ms for affected requests, and produced a sustained increase in token-costs for customers on bursty workloads.
impact:
- ~18% increase in per-token cost for affected routes during incident window
- Transient 95p latency regression (~320ms) for ~12k requests over 3 hours
- No customer data loss; a handful of customer-facing timeouts (approx 40) reported to SRE
- Internal error budget burn observed for dedicated capacity pools
timeline: 2026-03-09T02:07Z: First anomalous scaling event detected by autoscale-health alert (scale-flapping on api-prod-pool-7)
2026-03-09T02:10Z: Console graphs show repeated pod churn; triage page created and paged on-call
2026-03-09T02:22Z: Emergency heuristic rollback: temporarily increase HPA minReplicas from 2 to 4 for api-prod-pool-7 to stabilize latency
2026-03-09T03:05Z: Observed reduced 95p latency after temporary minReplica bump; however cost increased — rollback to previous setting at 03:30Z after mitigation plan discussed
2026-03-09T04:40Z: Root cause hypothesis formed: KEDA redis-stream scaler sampling window (10s) vs HPA custom metric window (60s) and percentile misinterpretation led to oscillatory scale signals
2026-03-10T09:00Z: Postmortem investigation kickoff; logs, metric histograms, request traces collected
2026-03-12T16:00Z: Reproduced an oscillation pattern with synthetic loadbench that mimics short 2–8s bursts; confirmed warm-pool assignment skew for model-shard replicas
2026-03-13T11:15Z: Drafted action items and stabilization playbook for prevention and long-term fixes
root_cause: A mismatch between high-frequency KEDA scaler sampling (10s) producing sharp, short-lived scale signals and the HPA aggregation/percentile window (60s) caused conflicting scale decisions. The HPA's percentile-based target picked up short outliers differently than KEDA, while our warm-pool allocation logic favored recently-evicted pods leading to ineffective warm pool reuse for certain model shard labels. Together these caused a feedback loop: KEDA triggered scale-ups, HPA saw variance and oscillated, nodes reclaimed capacity, and new pods experienced cold-loading of model weights.
mitigation_taken:
- Immediate: increased HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds from 30->90 and temporarily raised minReplicas for the impacted pool to reduce churn.
- Observability: added a short-term dashboard combining KEDA scaler events, HPA recommendations, and pod warm-pool hit-rates.
- Rollout: paused an in-flight KEDA scaler tuning change that reduced sampling smoothing (reverted PR).
action_items: Ravi Menon - implement signal fusion layer in autoscaler that harmonizes KEDA and HPA decisions with configurable hysteresis (due 2026-04-15)
Maya Chen - add percentile-aware smoothing to custom HPA exporter so short bursts are downweighted before aggregation (due 2026-04-08)
Platform - revise warm-pool matching to prefer 'model-shard' affinity and avoid recently-evicted labels; add unit + e2e tests for warm-pool reuse (owner: Platform Team, due 2026-04-22)
SRE - create runbook for transient scale-flapping that includes safe minReplica bump and rollback steps (owner: SRE Oncall, due 2026-03-20)
Observability - instrument 'warm-pool hit-rate' as a primary SLO for dedicated pools and add automated alert when <90% over 15m (owner: Observability, due 2026-03-27)
Docs - document recommended scaler configuration patterns for bursty inference workloads in runbooks + public KB (owner: DevRel, due 2026-04-05)
postmortem_notes: We discovered a blind spot: our autoscaler test harness did not include sub-10s burst traffic patterns common to interactive embeddings endpoints.
Warm-pool heuristics assumed uniform shard reuse; adaptive labeling for newer model shards is required.
Short-term stabilization choices traded cost for latency; long-term fix should preserve both.
Recommend adding synthetic chaos tests that randomly vary KEDA/HPA window parameters to detect brittle configurations before shipping changes.
